expectation: Membrane rings on a few scattered NK cells and a subset of CD8 T cells. These should be rare, single lymphocytes in the lamina propria or stroma, with a few in lymphoid aggregates or among intraepithelial lymphocytes. Most epithelial and stromal cells should be negative.
observed: A: the whole mucosa glows, following the gland and crypt architecture and tissue density; muscle is dimmer and there are bright lines at folds. B and C: diffuse haze over the epithelium and lamina propria with no distinct positive cells. D: an even glow around every nucleus.
why: The signal follows the tissue architecture and lights nearly every epithelial and stromal cell about alike, with no distinct sparse lymphocyte population.
notes: The yellow outlines the whole mucosa and glands like tissue autofluorescence or background. In the close-ups every cell is lit about the same and there are no separate ringed lymphocytes, so no specific NKG2A-positive population is visible.
